approach: Fix both origins and keep liveness defined by one signal (registry entry or held job lock). (A) In the run: `Athena::dispatch` commits the job record and brief (run/mod.rs:1249-1257); every later `?` returns Err with no outcome, which `RealSteps::run` maps to `Run{outcome: None}` (drain.rs:4395-4408). Wrap the post-commit section: an error that is not a deliberate hold (LowDisk, SlotWait, BudgetShort), with the kill switch off, no resume mark, and the job still Dispatched at HEAD, closes the job `failed` with a stated reason through the existing `close_dispatched`, booking only invocations that left a trace (`recover_traces`, split out of `recover_interrupted`, no synthesized producer). (B) In the listing: `steward::interrupted_work` keeps only the cli/steward channels (steward.rs:467) and hides every job that any later request retries (448-460), whatever became of that retry. Drop the channel filter for interrupted jobs only, reuse `reading::retries_by_job`, take liveness from a new `Athena::has_process(job)` (registry entry or job lock held; status.rs), and add a pure `steward::settle_interrupted(records, live, held, final_pass)` through a defaulted `Steps::settle_interrupted` hook, run before the queue view and after the sweep. It closes originals whose retry ended and reports every dispatched job still without an outcome as held with a reason. `status` already lists every dispatched job without a process; its only change is that a job whose lock another process holds shows as running. Ordering (finding 4): the six live jobs are closed or re-queued with today's `athena close` / `athena retry` BEFORE the new build runs its first drain, after listing every dispatched job with no outcome in today's `athena status`. Scope (findings 1-3): hestia.rs is no longer touched; the error-close core tests stay in run/tests.rs and the trace split in manage.rs, each justified below.

decisions.choice: Operator step first, before the new build is deployed or any drain runs on it. Run today's `athena status` (scan_jobs lists every Dispatched job with no registry entry as interrupted, on every channel), write the list down, and for each of the six read brief-producer.md and `git log`: where the work landed run `athena close <job> --why "landed through <job id> as <hash>"` (today's close works on a dispatched job with no process, manage.rs:145-157); otherwise `athena retry <job>` (g63s expected). Also close, with a reason, any other old interrupted job that the drain should not resurrect. If the list is long (more than a handful), close the clearly stale ones in a shell loop with `athena close <job> --why "stale before the drain change: <reason>"`, and leave deliberate ones; the first drain on the new build is bounded by `max_jobs`, the budget and ATTEMPTS = 2 per item (drain.rs:284), and every job it does not reach gets a `held <job>` note, so nothing is retried unseen.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. The new `interrupted_work` lists any Dispatched job with no process on any channel, unless `retries_by_job` finds a standing retry. A re-ask is not a retry for `retries_by_job` (reading/retry.rs:246-268), so msh3 and hvyb would be retried again, and old web-channel jobs would be listed for the first time. Today's `athena close` already does what the six need, so the new build is not required for them.

decisions.choice: Define 'no process' as `!running(job) && !job_lock_held(job)` through a new `Athena::has_process(&self, job:&str)->bool` in status.rs next to `running`. Pass `|j| athena.has_process(j)` to `interrupted_work`, `settle_interrupted` and `state_name`. `Athena::running` is unchanged.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 4 (earlier round) and 8. The name `has_process` avoids the clashes with `Steps::in_flight` (drain.rs:675), `in_flight_limit` (disk.rs) and `other_jobs_in_flight` (state.rs:169, which means lock held and work tree present). `running` checks only the registry (status.rs:885), but `go_job` holds the job lock for the whole of `dispatch` (run/mod.rs:443) and `Athena::retry` does not take the original's lock, so dropping the channel filter on a registry-only test could retry a live job. `StateDir::job_lock_held` (state.rs:153) is a probe that creates no lock file, and the codebase already uses the free lock as the liveness signal (disk.rs:188,233).

rejected.why: `go_job` holds its own lock and calls `running` (run/mod.rs:478, 539), so it would misreport itself; other callers (reading.rs:1060 and others) pin messages.

decisions.choice: Close a job whose run errors after the Dispatch commit, inside `dispatch`, as `failed` with reason `stopped by an error after dispatch, before the job closed: <redacted error>`, via the existing `close_dispatched` with a `Closing` whose `new_invocations` come from `recover_traces`. `close_after_error` skips (returns the original Err) when: (1) the error downcasts to LowDisk, SlotWait or BudgetShort; (2) `state.registry().stopped()`; (3) `state.read_resume(id)` is Some; (4) NEW, finding 7: the records reloaded at HEAD (`Records::load(&self.git, &self.head()?)`) show the job is no longer Dispatched (a closing, blocked or landing commit already exists); (5) the reload itself fails.

Condition (4) makes the guard explicit instead of relying on no `?` following a closing commit (close.rs:8-168, 244-460), so a later edit cannot produce a second outcome. `dispatch` holds the job lock, so `Athena::close` (manage.rs:96) cannot be called from there; `close_dispatched` can.

decisions.choice: New pure `steward::settle_interrupted(records, live, held, final_pass) -> Vec<Settlement>` (`Close{job,why}` / `Hold{job,why}`) through a defaulted `Steps::settle_interrupted(&self, final_pass: bool) -> Vec<String>`; `RealSteps` implements it with `Athena::close`. Population: `records.request_jobs()` in state Dispatched with `!live(job)`. Rules: (1) `held(job)` Some (disk or slot marker, `disk::read_any_hold`, run/mod.rs:481-490): Hold. (2) No request record (`athena retry` refuses it, retry.rs:54-56): Close 'dispatched with no request record; it cannot be retried'. (3) A standing retry, followed through interrupted retries to depth 16: last retry closed -> Close every interrupted job of the chain with `re-queued as <retry>, which ended <state>`; open -> Hold 'retried as <retry>, still <state>'. (4) No standing retry and `final_pass == false`: nothing. (5) No standing retry and `final_pass == true`: Hold 'dispatched with no outcome and no process; not worked in this drain (job limit, budget, stop, or its retry could not be read); `athena retry <job>` resumes it, `athena close <job> --why ...` closes it'.
decisions.reason: A pure function over `Records` is unit-tested without a model; a defaulted trait method leaves every test stub unedited, as `reclaim_interrupted` does (drain.rs:576). `Athena::close` recovers invocations, cleans and commits under the gate, and takes the job lock (manage.rs:96), so a live job is refused even if the probe raced.

risks.risk: The first drain on the new build retries every old interrupted job, the six included, and lists old off-channel jobs for the first time (finding 4).
risks.mitigation: Operator step first: list every dispatched job with no outcome with today's `athena status`, close or re-queue the six with today's `athena close` / `athena retry`, close stale others with a stated reason, and only then deploy. If the list is long, close the stale ones in a loop with a reason and leave deliberate ones; the first drain is bounded by `max_jobs`, budget and ATTEMPTS = 2 per item, and jobs it does not reach carry a `held` note.

risks.risk: The error close ends as failed a job that a later drain would have resumed, for example after a transient fault.
risks.mitigation: Only errors with no hold type, no kill switch, no resume mark and a job still Dispatched at HEAD are closed. The outcome is `failed`, so `athena retry` and the drain's second attempt can run it again from the request. A hold or a built candidate stays dispatched.

risks.risk: A later edit returns Err after a closing or blocked commit and the wrapper writes a second outcome (finding 7).
risks.mitigation: `close_after_error` reloads the records at HEAD and returns the original error unless the job is Dispatched; a core test closes a job first and shows no second outcome is written.

risks.risk: An infrastructure error counts as a failed job in introspection and the scope guard and could pause a line after repeated errors.
risks.mitigation: Matches the `stop_planning` precedent (planning.rs:8-14). The reason has a fixed prefix so a person can tell it from a verifier failure. Raised in open_questions.

risks.risk: Repeated failed retries of a request whose run errors the same way every time.
risks.mitigation: Existing bounds: ATTEMPTS = 2 per item per drain, no re-listing of a closed failed job, the scope guard pause, MAX_RETRY_DEPTH 16. The drain error test asserts at most two failed jobs and no new job from a second drain.

risks.risk: The drain retries or closes a live job another process runs.
risks.mitigation: `Athena::has_process` checks the registry and the job lock; it feeds the queue view, the settle and status. The settle's close goes through `Athena::close`, which takes the lock itself. A real-steps test holds the lock of an off-channel dispatched job with no registry entry and asserts it is neither retried, closed nor named in a held line.

risks.risk: The error close books a phantom producer at the producer cap.
risks.mitigation: The error close uses `recover_traces` only. The `recover_traces` unit test shows no traces yield no invocation, and a test keeps `recover_interrupted` synthesizing the producer for `athena close`. No end-to-end claim is made, since no hook fails before the producer spawn with planning off.

risks.risk: The reason text of the error carries a secret or a machine path.
risks.mitigation: The reason goes through `ctx.redactor.redact` before it is committed; if redaction fails, a fixed text without the error is used. A core test puts a path in the error.

risks.risk: `close_dispatched` itself fails, so the job stays dispatched.
risks.mitigation: The original error is returned with the second as context. The next drain lists the job and the final-pass settle reports it with a reason.

risks.risk: Closing an original too early could lose work or retry it twice.
risks.mitigation: Settle closes only when the standing retry (followed through interrupted retries) has an outcome; an open retry gives a Hold; a held job is never closed. Unit tests cover running, lock-held, held, open, closed and chained cases; a drain test asserts the retried original is not retried twice.

risks.risk: `retries_by_job` treats an abandoned retry as not standing, so closing a middle job could re-list its parent.
risks.mitigation: The settle follows the chain and closes every interrupted job in it in one pass, depth cap 16. A Z-A-B unit test covers it.

risks.risk: Resuming off-channel jobs reverses a documented rule and an existing test.
risks.mitigation: The rewrite is explicit and named in the CHANGELOG. `queued_work` keeps its filter, pinned by a new test. The change applies only to dispatched jobs with no registry entry and no held lock.

risks.risk: Closing during a parallel drain races with a worker.
risks.mitigation: Settle errors become notes and never fail the drain. `close` takes the job lock and refuses a job another process runs. The final call comes after `sweep`, when all workers have finished.

risks.risk: hestia.rs's private prefix constant drifts from the settle reason's literal prefix.
risks.mitigation: The literal is in one steward constant with a doc comment naming hestia.rs:342, pinned by a steward test; the effect of drift is limited to the review waiting for a newer introspection (hestia.rs:317-320). Residual risk accepted to keep hestia.rs out of the diff.

risks.risk: The `interrupt` helper leaves the history one commit short, unlike a real process death.
risks.mitigation: The `interrupt` helper is used only for the restart shape, and its tests assert before the drain that the job has no invocation and no outcome. The error-path tests use the real code path with a planner-role trigger and assert after the drain (no pre-drain moment exists there). `go_with_disk` (tests/drain.rs:2424) covers the hold case.

risks.risk: A planning-on Fixture builder in tests/drain.rs may need more scripting than expected.
risks.mitigation: If the Fixture cannot take the `[job_plan]` block as job_plan.rs:85 does, the drain-level error test is dropped and the core error test in run/tests.rs plus the `interrupt`-based drain tests carry criterion 1; the producer reports it.

risks.risk: The six outcomes cannot be written by the diff because records/ is excluded.
risks.mitigation: The diff holds code, tests and CHANGELOG only. Demonstration 4 is an operator step with each close citing a hash read from git log; it needs write access to the live records.

risks.risk: Settle's `Athena::close` books a Missing producer at the cap for an original that never ran a producer.
risks.mitigation: This is what a person's `athena close` does today and keeps the cost bound honest for a dead process; noted in the CHANGELOG.

demonstrations.method: Four layers, each stopping a dispatched job before the producer runs and driving a production entry point. (1) Core: `Athena::go` with `repo_with_planning(1)`; the planner-role script plants the blocking `records` file so the first invocation fails after the Dispatch commit. (2) Drain, real steps: a cli job and a web job stopped with `interrupt` (asserted dispatched, no invocation, no outcome before the drain), then `drain::drain`; and the planner-role error job in a planning-on Fixture. (3) A job whose lock is held with no registry entry. (4) steward `settle_*` and `interrupted_work` unit tests, plus the manage.rs `recover_traces` unit tests.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core run::tests::an_error_after_dispatch && cargo test --locked -p athena-core manage::tests::recover_traces && cargo test --locked -p athena-core steward::tests && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain -- interrupted after_dispatch
demonstrations.observes: Core: `go` returns Finished with state Failed and a reason starting `stopped by an error after dispatch`; the job has job.json and brief-producer.md, a recovered planner invocation and no producer invocation; a low-disk hold, a kill-switch stop and an already-closed job are left as they were (original Err returned). manage.rs: `recover_traces` on a directory with no traces returns nothing; with a live record and a usage file it returns both; `recover_interrupted` still synthesizes the Missing producer for a job with no traces. Drain: the cli and the web original both end Closed(Abandoned) with a reason starting `re-queued as <retry>`; the planner-error job ends Closed(Failed) in the same drain with the reason in the report, has at most two failed jobs per request, and a second drain dispatches nothing. The lock-held job is not retried, not named in a `held <job>` note and stays Dispatched. Steward: held is Hold, request-less is Close, open retry is Hold, closed retry is Close, dropped retry gives no settle but is listed by `interrupted_work`, running or lock-held gives nothing, chain Z-A-B closes both, `final_pass` false gives nothing and true gives a Hold with a reason.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the dispatch wrapper `go` returns Err and the job stays dispatched with no outcome, so the core and drain error tests fail. Without the new `interrupted_work` the web job is not listed and stays dispatched, a job whose retry was dropped is never re-listed, and a job whose retry landed stays dispatched. Without the lock probe the live off-channel job is retried and the lock test fails. Without the Dispatched-at-HEAD check, the test that makes the closing already committed (a script-free core test that calls `close_after_error` on a closed job through `go` with a second Err injected after `finish_dispatched` is not available, so this one is covered by the explicit unit test of `close_after_error` on a reloaded closed job) would write a second outcome. The phantom-producer case is covered only by the `recover_traces` unit test, which fails if the synthesis moves into it.

open_questions: User: May a job that was interrupted and whose standing retry ended rejected or failed be closed as abandoned with the reason `re-queued as <retry>, which ended <state>`? The plan does so, because the retry carries the work forward and the original would otherwise stay dispatched for ever. The alternative is to leave it listed as 'retried as X' until a person closes it.

User: Should an error after dispatch with no kept candidate close the job as `failed` (retryable, counted by introspection and the scope guard, as `stop_planning` does) or as `abandoned` (not counted, but `athena retry` refuses it)? The plan uses `failed`.

User: May the diff include crates/athena-core/src/manage.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs although they are not listed deliverables? The plan keeps them (the trace split and the only fixtures for the error-close and hold-skip tests) and drops hestia.rs; without them the error close would either book a phantom producer or lose invocation cost.
